data.text:
Typhoon Co-May (#EmongPH) has clipped the Bolinao Peninsula in the Philippines at 75 mph (120 kph), whipping the towns in the region with heavy rain and wind overnight. The storm is now nocturnally slinking up the coast and closing in on landfall in NW Luzon. Fortunately, Co-May has not continued to strengthen as initially forecast, and instead has leveled out in intensity due to interaction with Luzon’s mountains. Of course, this same land interaction is also sparking big convective bursts, so be on alert for possible flooding if you’re in this area. 

(Sat-image credit: weathernerds)

Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 61 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Enhanced Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) and Typhoon EMONG
Issued at: 5:00 AM, 25 July 2025(Friday)

ORANGE WARNING LEVEL: Zambales and Bataan.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING is still THREATENING.

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Rizal, Metro Manila, Laguna, Cavite and Batangas.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Nueva Ecija and Quezon(Real, General Nakar, Infanta) which may persist within 3 hours and may affect nearby areas.
The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 8:00 AM today.

For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZISbP.

**🌊 Typhoon Co-May Batters Bolinao: Stay Safe Amid Flood Risks! 🌧️**

Typhoon Co-May (#EmongPH) hit the Bolinao Peninsula, PHILIPPINES with 75 mph (120 kph) winds, unleashing heavy rain overnight. Now tracking along NW Luzon’s coast, it’s held back by the region’s terrain but still threatens flooding from intense convective bursts. 🌪️💦 Protect yourself and the environment—stay informed, avoid flood-prone areas, and preserve our ecosystems! 🌏 #TyphoonEmongPH #EnvironmentalSafety #SaveNature
